title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Visits Sainya Sampark Mela in Deoghar, Jharkhand
subtitle:
“Our Soldiers Have Always Stood with the Nation, and We Must Always Stand with Them and Their Families”: Vice-President

Vice-President Calls for Continued National Commitment to Welfare of Veterans and Veer Naris

Jharkhand Has a Proud Tradition of Military Service and Sacrifice: Vice-President
date:
Posted On:
                10 OCT 2026 5:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, visited the Sainya Sampark Mela – Sadaiv Aapke Saath in Deoghar, Jharkhand, today. The Mela was organised by the Indian Army in collaboration with the Deoghar District Administration to provide welfare services and grievance redressal facilities to ex-servicemen, Veer Naris and their dependents across the Santhal Pargana region.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan visited the Sainya Sampark Mela – Sadaiv Aapke Saath in Deoghar, Jharkhand, organised by the Indian Army to support veterans, Veer Naris and their families.

He emphasised that while our soldiers have always stood with the Nation, the Nation must always stand with them and their families. He called for a lasting national commitment to their welfare, ensuring that their sacrifices are honoured and they receive the respect, support and care they deserve.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
October 10, 2026
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President paid tribute to the veterans and Veer Naris for their invaluable sacrifices and contributions to the Nation. Describing veterans as an important national resource, he said that their experience could guide the youth and their leadership could contribute significantly to nation-building. Saluting the Veer Naris, he observed that behind every soldier serving at the border stands a family that shares the sacrifices and responsibilities of military service. He emphasised that the Nation could never forget the sacrifices made by soldiers and their families.
Recalling his tenure as Governor of Jharkhand, the Vice-President highlighted the State’s proud tradition of service to the Nation. He paid tribute to Param Vir Chakra awardee Lance Naik Albert Ekka and recalled the contributions of tribal freedom fighters, including Bhagwan Birsa Munda, Tilka Manjhi, Sidhu and Kanhu, and Nilambar and Pitambar. He said that the spirit of patriotism and national service continued to inspire the people of Jharkhand.
The Vice-President highlighted the fulfilment of the long-standing demand for One Rank, One Pension under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and referred to various welfare initiatives undertaken for veterans and Veer Naris. Appreciating the single-window mechanism at the Mela, he said that bringing pension-related assistance, medical facilities, documentation services and grievance redressal under one platform was a meaningful example of last-mile delivery.
Emphasising the importance of coordinated public service, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that the participation of the Armed Forces, civil administration, financial institutions, healthcare providers and welfare agencies reflected a shared commitment to serving those who had served the Nation. He called for the theme “Sadaiv Aapke Saath” (Always with You) to become a continuing national commitment, ensuring that veterans and their families always felt respected, supported and cared for.
During the visit, the Vice-President toured various stalls at the Sainya Sampark Mela, including displays of weapons and military equipment, disaster relief facilities, Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS) services, medical screening and blood donation camps, women’s health awareness initiatives, NCC activities and pension-related services. He also interacted with veterans, beneficiaries and other people attending the Mela.
The Vice-President congratulated the Indian Army and the Deoghar District Administration for organising the initiative and appreciated the efforts of Member of Parliament Dr. Nishikant Dubey. He also thanked the participating institutions and agencies for their contributions towards the welfare of the Armed Forces community.
The event was attended by the Governor of Jharkhand, Shri Santosh Kumar Gangwar; Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav; Members of Parliament Dr. Nishikant Dubey and Shri Aditya Sahu; General Officer Commanding, 111 Area, Lt. Gen. Pawan Chadha; Chairperson of Baba Baidyanath Medical Trust, Ms. Anamika Gautam; senior officers of the Indian Army, officials of the civil administration, veterans, Veer Naris and their families.

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Addresses Second Convocation of AIIMS Deoghar
subtitle:
“Let Your Knowledge Heal, Your Research Innovate and Your Service Inspire”: Vice-President to Young Graduates

Vice-President Urges Young Medical Professionals to Make Competence, Compassion and Character Their Guiding Principles

“Access to Quality Healthcare and Higher Education for Tribal and Rural Communities Is Central to the Vision of Viksit Bharat”: Vice-President

“AIIMS Deoghar Reflects the Vision of Balanced and Inclusive Development”: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 OCT 2026 2:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today addressed the Second Convocation of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Deoghar, Jharkhand, and congratulated the graduating doctors, nurses and healthcare professionals. Describing the convocation as a celebration of the aspirations of the Santhal Pargana region, he said that AIIMS Deoghar symbolises the growing opportunities in medical education and healthcare for tribal and rural communities.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the Second Convocation of AIIMS Deoghar in Jharkhand today. 

Highlighting AIIMS Deoghar as a symbol of balanced and inclusive development, the Vice-President emphasised that access to quality healthcare and medical education must reach every corner of the country.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
October 10, 2026
Highlighting the legacy of Bhagwan Birsa Munda, Sidho-Kanhu and Tilka Manjhi, the Vice-President urged the graduates to carry their knowledge beyond institutional boundaries and serve villages, tribal communities and the most remote parts of the country. He said that the highest meaning of medical knowledge lies in service to society, and called upon the young professionals to uphold competence, integrity, empathy and ethical conduct. He emphasised that a medical degree is not merely an achievement but an obligation to serve the underserved and vulnerable with compassion and dedication.
The Vice-President appreciated AIIMS Deoghar’s contribution to strengthening regional healthcare. He commended its community outreach initiatives covering malaria elimination, lymphatic filariasis surveillance, anaemia, hearing health and school health, noting that the responsibility of a medical institution extends well beyond its campus.
Referring to the expansion of medical education and healthcare infrastructure under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President said that the number of medical colleges in the country has increased from 387 before 2014 to 846. He said that institutions such as AIIMS Deoghar reflect the commitment to balanced and inclusive development. Access to quality healthcare and higher education in every State, district and village, he emphasised, is essential to realising the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.
The Vice-President noted with satisfaction that women constituted 132 of the 173 graduating students. He said this reflected the country’s progress from women’s empowerment towards women-led development and underscored the transformative role of education in enabling women to realise their potential.
Addressing the graduates, the Vice-President urged them to remain connected to the communities the Institute was established to serve, embrace emerging technologies responsibly, and ensure that advances in artificial intelligence, telemedicine and digital diagnostics benefit people in remote areas as well as cities. He also called upon them to champion a “No to Drugs” message among young people and commended nursing professionals for their essential role in providing compassionate patient care.
The Vice-President expressed confidence that the Institute would continue to grow as a centre of clinical excellence, scientific research and compassionate service to Jharkhand and the wider eastern region. He concluded by urging the graduates to make competence, compassion and character the guiding principles of their professional lives and contribute meaningfully to the making of a Viksit Bharat.
The convocation was attended by the Governor of Jharkhand, Shri Santosh Kumar Gangwar; Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav; Jharkhand Minister for Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare, Dr. Irfan Ansari; Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha), Dr. Nishikant Dubey; Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha), Shri Pradip Kumar Varma; Deoghar MLA, Shri Suresh Paswan; President of AIIMS Deoghar, Professor M. V. Padma Srivastava; and Executive Director and CEO of AIIMS Deoghar, Professor Nitin M. Gangane, among other dignitaries, faculty members, graduating students and their families.

title: PM to Visit Chennai on 11 October
subtitle:
PM to Lay Foundation Stone, Inaugurate and Dedicate Development Projects Worth Over ₹13,000 Crore in Chennai

Projects Span Metro Rail, Highways, Railways, Ports, Petroleum and Education Sectors

PM to Inaugurate Poonamallee-Vadapalani Stretch of Phase II of Chennai Metro Rail Project

PM to Lay Foundation Stone and Inaugurate National Highway Projects Worth Around ₹3,700 Crore in Tamil Nadu

PM to Inaugurate and Lay Foundation Stones for Port Projects at Chennai Port, Kamarajar Port and V.O. Chidambaranar Port

PM to inaugurate five Amrit Stations at Palani, Vellore Cantonment, Ambasamudram, Paramakkudi and Namakkal

PM to dedicate to the nation the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras

PM to Participate in Golden Jubilee Celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School

PM to Perform Darshan and Pooja at Jalakandeswarar Temple in Chennai
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 OCT 2026 12:46PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit Chennai, Tamil Nadu, on 11 October. At around 11:30 AM, he will undertake a ride on the Chennai Metro from Porur Bypass Station to Poonamallee Bypass Station and back. At around 12:15 PM, he will perform Darshan and Pooja at the Jalakandeswarar Temple in Chennai. Thereafter, he will undertake a walkthrough of the Brain Centre at IIT Madras.
At around 1:30 PM, the Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of, inaugurate and dedicate various development projects worth over ₹13,000 crore. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. At around 3 PM, he will participate in the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School in Chennai and address the gathering.
Prime Minister will inaugurate the Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around ₹4,900 crore. The corridor features a unique 3.7-km double-decker structure. It also features advanced signalling systems designed to support driverless operations. It is expected to reduce daily travel time for commuters and improve connectivity between Chennai’s rapidly growing western suburbs and the city centre.
Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of and inaugurate key National Highway projects worth around ₹3,700 crore. These projects will strengthen road connectivity, reduce travel time, ease traffic congestion and support economic growth in the State.
Prime Minister will inaugurate the 36-km, four-laned Vadugapatti-Therkuvenganallur section of NH-744. The project will improve connectivity to important pilgrimage, industrial and commercial centres in the region, facilitating smoother movement of people and goods. He will also inaugurate the 30-km, four-laned Madurai Ring Road section of NH-744A. The project will improve traffic movement around Madurai and help ease congestion within the city.
Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of the four-lane Thiruvarur Bypass on the Nagapattinam-Thanjavur section of NH-83. The project will strengthen road connectivity in Thiruvarur and facilitate smoother traffic movement by providing an alternative route around the town.
Prime Minister will dedicate and inaugurate railway infrastructure projects worth over ₹750 crore. He will dedicate the Karaikal-Peralam railway line, further strengthening rail connectivity in the region. He will also dedicate three rail flyovers in Coimbatore and surrounding areas. These will ease congestion at busy level crossings, reduce waiting time and improve road safety for commuters. Prime Minister will also inaugurate five Amrit Stations at Palani, Vellore Cantonment, Ambasamudram, Paramakkudi and Namakkal, which have been redeveloped under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme.
Prime Minister will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of several port-related projects in Tamil Nadu to strengthen maritime infrastructure, expand cargo-handling capacity and improve logistics efficiency.
Prime Minister will inaugurate four infrastructure projects at Chennai Port: a Paved Storage Yard, four EXIM Godowns, an upgraded Cruise Terminal and a Seafarers Club. These projects will improve cargo storage and handling, expand warehouse capacity, modernise passenger facilities to enable the simultaneous embarkation and disembarkation of more cruise passengers, and provide modern welfare, recreational and support facilities for visiting seafarers and maritime personnel.  Prime Minister will inaugurate and lay the foundation stones for eight major development projects at V.O. Chidambaranar Port. The projects will expand cargo and container capacity, building infrastructure for the transition to cleaner maritime energy, and improving the efficiency of cargo evacuation and logistics within the Port ecosystem. Prime Minister will also inaugurate the Coal Berth-3 project and lay the foundation stone for capital dredging works for Container Terminal Phase-I, Stage-II at Kamarajar Port.
Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of the Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks (LOBS) project at the existing Manali Refinery of Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL) in Chennai. With a total cost of around ₹1,620 crore and a capacity of 270 thousand metric tonnes per annum (TMTPA), the project aims to produce Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks for the manufacture of world-class, premium-quality lubricants in India.
Prime Minister will dedicate to the nation the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre (SGBC) at IIT Madras. He will also launch its pioneering global scientific mission to map more than 100 human brains into three-dimensional atlases at cellular resolution, across the human lifespan - from the foetal stage to old age. Prime Minister will also release C-STROKE, a one-of-its-kind human ischaemic stroke atlas. Featuring over 1,000 annotated microscopic sections from a stroke-affected brain, the atlas will help researchers worldwide identify novel therapeutic targets.
Prime Minister will participate in the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School in Chennai. The Golden Jubilee marks five decades of the institution’s contribution to education and its role in nurturing  generations of students through academic excellence, discipline, cultural values and holistic education. Guided by its motto, “Sa Vidya Ya Vimuktaye” (Knowledge that liberates), the school seeks to nurture individuals who make meaningful contributions to society. Over the years, the institution has evolved in response to changing educational needs while continuing to place strong emphasis on character-building, knowledge and responsible citizenship.

title: The Indian Parliamentary Delegation, led by Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, continued its participation in the 153rd Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) Assembly in Arusha, Tanzania, on the fifth and final day of the Assembly, 9 October 2026.
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 OCT 2026 1:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Shri Harivansh and Members of the Delegation attended the meeting of the Governing Council of the IPU, which took up the remaining agenda items, including the election of the President of the Inter-Parliamentary Union and reports of specialised meetings.
Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha; Shri Anurag Singh Thakur, MP, Lok Sabha; and Smt. Kamaljeet Sehrawat, MP, Lok Sabha, cast the three votes allocated to India in the election of the President of the Inter-Parliamentary Union.
Following the election by secret ballot, the incumbent IPU President declared Mr. Milton Dick, Speaker of the House of Representatives of Australia, elected as the next President of the IPU. Immediately after the announcement of the result, Shri Harivansh and other Members of the Indian Parliamentary Delegation congratulated Mr. Dick in person and wished him a successful tenure as President of the IPU.
Subsequently, Dr. Sasmit Patra, MP, Rajya Sabha, presented to Mr. Milton Dick a congratulatory letter from the Hon’ble Speaker, Lok Sabha.
After the conclusion of the Governing Council meeting, the Assembly held its sittings to adopt the Arusha Communiqué; the resolution submitted by the Standing Committee on Democracy and Human Rights on “Inclusive social development for all: Parliamentary strategies to promote the rights and empowerment of persons with disabilities”; and the resolution on the emergency item, “Urgent parliamentary action to address climate-related disasters and strengthen resilience in the Himalayan region and other vulnerable regions”.
Thereafter, H.E. Mussa Azzan Zungu, Speaker of the National Assembly of Tanzania and President of the Assembly, declared the Assembly closed.
The Indian Parliamentary Delegation, led by Shri Harivansh, Hon’ble Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, participated in the 153rd IPU Assembly held in Arusha, Tanzania, from 5 to 9 October 2026. The Delegation’s participation was eventful and effective, and it contributed to the resolutions and outcomes of the IPU Assembly.

title: Young Innovators showcase their talent in ‘Robotics for Good Youth Challenge India 2026’ hosted by Department of Telecommunications (DoT) and International Telecommunication Union (ITU) during India Mobile Congress 2026
subtitle:
Team Singularity and Ferrum Incubators emerge as Junior and Senior Champions; to represent India at the Global Grand Finale in Geneva in 2027

Event organised by the I-Hub Foundation for Cobotics (IHFC),  Technology Innovation Hub (TIH) of IIT Delhi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 OCT 2026 11:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Robotics for Good Youth Challenge India 2026–2027, organised by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India with the support of the I-Hub Foundation for Cobotics (IHFC), Technology Innovation Hub (TIH) of IIT Delhi, was held today on the sidelines of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi.
The Challenge, a flagship initiative under ITU’s AI for Good programme, brought together 57 teams – 28 in the Junior Category and 29 in the Senior Category – with around 300 students and mentors from 14 States across India. Students aged 10 to 18 designed, built and programmed autonomous robots to address this year’s mission on public health emergency response, linked to United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) 3 – Good Health and Well-being, through tasks such as sample extraction and delivery, construction of a quarantine zone, medical-kit distribution and medical triage.
The Challenge was inaugurated by Mr. Atul Sinha, Director General, National Communications Academy-Technology (NCA-T), DoT, who delivered the inaugural keynote address, preceded by Dr Bilel Jamoussi, Deputy Director and Chief, Study Groups and Policy Department, Telecommunication Standardization Bureau, ITU, who delivered the welcome address.
The other distinguished speakers were Ashutosh Dutt Sharma, Chief Executive Officer, IHFC, TIH of IIT Delhi, Rama Krishna K, Assistant Professor, Department of Mechanical Engineering, IIT Delhi; Atman Jadon, Co-founder and CEO, Superceuticals Private Limited.
The journey began with registrations opening from 10–25 August 2026, inviting teams to take part in an exciting challenge of innovation, design and problem-solving. From 7–16 September 2026, teams participated in awareness and orientation programmes to understand the competition and submitted their design documents and videos for the preliminary round. As the excitement built, Practice Day on 9 October 2026 gave teams the opportunity to test their solutions on the competition game board, identify challenges and fine-tune their strategies ahead of the big day. The journey culminated in the India Nationals on 10 October 2026, where teams competed through two qualifying rounds, a knockout round and the final.
The Challenge encourages teamwork, problem-solving under pressure, project planning and meeting deadlines, and responsible and sustainable approaches to robot design. It also promotes inclusive access to robotics through the use of free software and hardware, so that participation is not restricted to students with expensive kits.
At the Closing and Award Ceremony, awards were presented to the winning teams in both categories by the dignitaries, along with special awards for Design, Innovation and Creative Thinking.
Senior Category:
Winner – Team Ferrum Incubators (Cambridge School, Noida, Uttar Pradesh); First Runner-up – Team Mech Minds (Lions Calcutta Greater Vidya Mandir, West Bengal); Second Runner-up – Team Botics Alpha (Vidya Pratishthan’s Magarpatta City Public School, Maharashtra).
Junior Category:
Winner – Team Singularity (Gopalan International School, Karnataka); First Runner-up – Team Veda Velocity (MSB Education Institute, Pune); Second Runner-up – Team Vajra (IgnAlte Robotics LLP, Uttar Pradesh).
The ceremony was addressed by Dr Bilel Jamoussi, Deputy Director and Chief, Study Groups and Policy Department, Telecommunication Standardization Bureau, ITU, who delivered the welcome address; Mr Ananda Raj Khanal, Head of the Regional Office for Asia & the Pacific; Shri Mukesh Kumar, Deputy Director General (International Relations), DoT; Prof. Subir Kumar Saha, Project Director, IHFC, TIH of IIT Delhi. This was followed by a session on Safe Cyberspace by Ms Diksha Dhiman, ADET (AI & DIU), DoT. The award distribution also witnessed Shri Hemendra Kumar Sharma, Counsellor and Technical Expert, Permanent Mission of India to the UN, along with the dignitaries, and the ceremony concluded with a vote of thanks by Mr. Piyush Prasad, Vice President and Head IHFC, TIH of IIT Delhi.
The winner teams of Junior and Senior category will represent India at the Grand Finale in Geneva, Switzerland, during the AI for Good Global Summit in June 2027, among participating countries. The dignitaries congratulated the winners, finalists and all participating teams, and appreciated the contribution of schools, coaches, mentors and families.
India and ITU share a longstanding partnership in telecommunications and technology. The Robotics for Good Youth Challenge India began in 2024, when the first Challenge was held during the World Telecommunication Standardization Assembly (WTSA-24) hosted by India, and has continued since then, with editions held at IMC 2025 and IMC 2026. It reflects the sustained collaboration among an international organisation, Government, academia and the innovation ecosystem to create opportunities for young innovators at national and international levels. It reinforced the message that participation itself is an achievement, and encouraged students to continue building, experimenting and solving real-world problems with technology that is safe, responsible and built for good.

title: Second Meeting of Global Initiative on AI for Agri-Food Systems (GI-AI4FS) held at IMC 2026 in New Delhi
subtitle: Meeting focuses on responsible and effective application of AI and IoT to transform agri-food systems
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 OCT 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Telecommunication Engineering Centre (TEC), Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India hosted the Second meeting of the UN Global Initiative on AI for Agri-Food Systems (GI-AI4FS) alongside India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026. The meeting was jointly hosted with Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India. The GI-AI4FS is a UN Global Initiative, coordinated by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), in close collaboration with Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) and World Food Programme (WFP).
The meeting witnessed active participation from around 70 delegates in-person and 25 participants online, bringing together representatives of international organisations, government departments, agricultural research institutions, academia, industry and standards development organisations to advance global cooperation on the application of Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in agriculture and food systems.
The inaugural session commenced with opening remarks by Dr. Sebastian Bosse, Chair of GI-AI4FS, followed by keynote addresses by Mr. Krishnan Pallassana, Senior Specialist – Strategy, Innovation & Partnerships, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), Dr. Bilel Jamoussi, Deputy Director, Telecommunication Standardization Bureau (TSB), ITU; Dr. A. K. Nayak, Deputy Director General (Natural Resource Management), ICAR, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare; Mr. Syed Tausif Abbas, Senior Deputy Director General & Head, TEC, DoT, India.
The meeting highlighted the growing role of AI, the Internet of Things (IoT) and digital connectivity in transforming agricultural practices and strengthening agri-food systems. The integration of connected sensors, weather stations, drones, satellite-based systems and AI-enabled analytics can support precision agriculture, improve resource utilisation, enable early detection of crop diseases and help farmers make informed decisions. Digital technologies also offer opportunities to improve traceability, reduce post-harvest losses and enhance efficiency across agricultural supply chains.
This meeting was preceded by a 2-day International Hackathon on ‘AI for Agri-Food Systems’, held on 8–9 October 2026, also jointly hosted by TEC, DoT and ICAR at the ICAR campus, New Delhi. The hackathon provided a collaborative platform for students, researchers, developers and innovators to develop practical technology solutions addressing real-world challenges in agriculture and food systems.
The GI-AI4FS meeting further featured a showcase of outcomes from this International Hackathon on AI Innovation for Resilient Agri-Food Systems. Shortlisted teams presented their solutions and demonstrated innovative AI applications developed during the hackathon. The programme also included the presentation of winning solutions and recognition of outstanding innovations, along with an award ceremony acknowledging the contributions of participating teams, partners, mentors and other contributors.
The meeting also addressed the governance architecture and organisational development of GI-AI4FS. The agenda included deliberations on the proposed governance and coordination structure, the nomination and confirmation of Working Group (WG) Chairs and Co-Chairs and members, the Terms of Reference of the Working Groups and the identification of priority areas and initial work streams.
Overall, the second meeting of GI-AI4FS provided a platform for advancing dialogue on the responsible use of AI in agriculture and food systems by promoting trustworthy and interoperable farmer-centric AI solutions, strengthening international cooperation on governance and standards and identifying opportunities to translate innovation into practical applications.

title: Minister of State for Coal and Mines inaugurates Third National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026)
subtitle:
Economic progress acquired its fullest meaning when its benefits are reflected in “stronger communities, wider opportunity and more resilient regions”- MoS, Satish Chandra Dubey

CSR represented an important expression of the collective effort required for Viksit Bharat: Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Dr. Pallavi Jain Govil
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 OCT 2026 4:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, Minister of State, Ministry of Coal and Mines, Government of India, inaugurated the Third National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026), organised by Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), under Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in New Delhi. The two-day Conference, scheduled on 6–7 October 2026, was organised around the theme “Re-envisioning the Spirit of CSR for Viksit Bharat: From Compliance to Commitment.”
In his Keynote Address, Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, Minister of State for Coal and Mines, emphasised the close relationship between national economic growth, regional development and the well-being of communities in resource-bearing areas. He observed that economic progress acquired its fullest meaning when its benefits were reflected in “stronger communities, wider opportunity and more resilient regions”.
He underlined that, for sectors closely connected with natural resources and local communities, growth and social development could not be viewed as separate objectives. On the occasion, he formally released the Comprehensive CSR Framework for Indian Coal Companies, developed to provide sector-specific direction for more structured, need-based and outcome-oriented CSR interventions in the coal sector.
The inaugural session also witnessed the release of the India CSR Factbook 2024–25, providing a consolidated reference on the evolving CSR landscape in India. The session was graced by
Dr. Pallavi Jain Govil
,
Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India
; Ms. Shoko Ishikawa, UN Women Country Representative in India;
Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh
,
Director General & CEO, IICA
; and
Prof. Garima Dadhich
,
Head, School of Business Environment, IICA
.
Delivering the Inaugural Address,
Smt. Pallavi Jain Govil
,
Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs
, placed CSR within India’s larger corporate-governance and national-development framework. She stated that the theme of NCCSR 2026 called upon stakeholders to “look beyond the annual obligation” and consider the larger contribution that responsible enterprise could make to India’s development journey. Referring to India’s distinctive statutory CSR architecture, she emphasised that the framework combined statutory obligation with company-level responsibility, Board oversight, public disclosure and impact assessment, and that CSR represented an important expression of the collective effort required for
Viksit Bharat
. She also released the
India CSR Factbook 2024–25
.
In his Welcome Address,
Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh
,
Director General & CEO, IICA
, highlighted the importance of keeping CSR discussions anchored in implementation and visible development outcomes. Noting that CSR brought together Government, industry, public sector enterprises, implementing organisations, development partners and academia, he observed that “decisions may be taken in Board rooms, but their value is ultimately seen in schools, health centres, livelihood programmes, villages, towns and districts where they affect the lives of people”. He said that the National CSR Exhibition had been designed not merely to display projects but to make outcomes visible and to serve as a space for learning, replication and partnership.
The inaugural session was followed by a fireside chat on “
Social Stock Exchange: Purpose, Capital & Impact
”, featuring
Shri Shailesh K. Pathak
, Senior Advisor – Policy, National Stock Exchange, and
Prof. Garima Dadhich
. The discussion examined the role of the Social Stock Exchange in connecting social purpose with capital and the importance of credible impact measurement, transparency and institutional trust in strengthening the social sector financing ecosystem.
In the post-lunch session,
Shri Ansuman Pattnaik
,
Additional Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India
, delivered the keynote address. His address placed CSR in the wider context of corporate governance and emphasised the need for companies to approach CSR as an integral part of responsible corporate conduct and institutional decision-making. He also invited companies to register on the CSR Exchange Portal, highlighting its relevance as a mechanism for connecting CSR stakeholders and facilitating purposeful engagement.
The keynote address was followed by High-Level Panel discussion on “
Board Governance and Strategic Commitment in CSR
”. The panel discussed the role of Boards and senior management in ensuring strategic oversight of CSR, the importance of linking expenditure with clearly identified needs and outcomes, and the need for effective monitoring and accountability mechanisms.
The panel comprised Shri Ashok Kumar Gupta (Retd.), CEO, Dalmia Bharat Foundation and former Chairperson, Competition Commission of India and National Financial Reporting Authority; Prof. Maneesha V. Ramesh, Pro Vice Chancellor, Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham; Shri Bhaskar Chowdary Nettem, Director (Production), ONGC; Shri Ayush Gupta, Director (Human Resources), GAIL (India) Limited; Shri Bibhuti Ranjan Pradhan, Executive Director (Coordination and CSR), Indian Oil Corporation Limited; Dr. Purvi Mehta, Independent Director, Mahindra Agri Solutions Limited; and Ms. Ruchi Sadhana, Vice President, HCLTech.
The discussions underlined that stronger Board engagement could improve the quality of CSR decision-making by ensuring closer attention to project relevance, implementation capacity, geographic and thematic need, monitoring, evaluation and sustainability. The panel also noted the value of partnerships and professional institutional mechanisms in translating CSR commitments into durable development outcomes.
The second Panel discussion on “
Sector-Based Approaches to CSR Aligned with SDG Priorities
” examined the case for closer alignment between CSR interventions, sectoral development priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals. The session was chaired by
Ms. Anita Shah Akella
,
Joint Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India
. In her keynote address, she underlined the need for sector-specific approaches that recognise differing development challenges, institutional capacities and local priorities.
The panel included Shri Lucas L. Kamsuan, Joint Secretary, Department of Public Enterprises, Government of India; Ms. Reetu Jain, Economic Adviser, Ministry of Power, Government of India; Dr. Chetna Shukla, Deputy Director General, Ministry of Coal, Government of India; Ms. Ruchika Gupta, Deputy Director General, Social Statistics Division, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Government of India; Shri Rajeev Kumar, Deputy Director General (Data & Management), Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Government of India; and Shri Prabhakar L., EVP & Head – Social Investments, ITC. Shri Bharat Wakhlu, Founder and President, The Wakhlu Advisory, moderated the session.
The panel deliberated on the need to move beyond uniform approaches to CSR and to recognise the distinct development contexts, operational footprints and stakeholder needs associated with different sectors by highlighting the significance of
sector-specific CSR frameworks developed by IICA for the Ministry of Coal and Coal India Limited
, in addressing sectoral development priorities and community needs. Additionally, it emphasised the need to
strengthen CSR reporting through alignment with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
, enabling systematic assessment of corporate contributions to national and global development priorities.
First day sessions concluded with a broad consensus on the need to strengthen the institutional quality of CSR—from Board-level oversight and evidence-based project selection to sectoral alignment, convergence, monitoring and assessment of outcomes. The proceedings reflected the Conference theme by placing emphasis on a transition from compliance alone towards sustained corporate commitment to inclusive and measurable development.
The Conference brought together senior representatives of the Government of India, public sector enterprises, private sector companies, international organisations, academia and civil society to deliberate on the evolving role of Corporate Social Responsibility in supporting national development priorities. The deliberations emphasised the need for CSR interventions to be guided by institutional responsibility, local development needs, measurable outcomes and effective convergence among stakeholders.
NCCSR 2026 is being organised by the
School of Business Environment
, IICA, with participation from Government, public sector enterprises, corporate organisations, international institutions, academia and civil society.

title: Third National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026) concludes, calls for stronger governance, convergence and outcome-oriented CSR for Viksit Bharat
subtitle: CSR is not merely as a statutory obligation but as a strategic instrument for India’s growth: Ajit Seth, former Cabinet Secretary, Govt of India
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 OCT 2026 4:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The
Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA)
,
Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India
, concluded the
Third National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026)
at
The Ashok, New Delhi
. The two-day Conference, organised by the
School of Business Environment, IICA
, was held under the theme “
Re-envisioning the Spirit of CSR for Viksit Bharat: From Compliance to Commitment
.”
The Conference concluded with the formal
Valedictory Session on “From Compliance to Commitment”
, in the presence of
Shri Ajit Seth
, former Cabinet Secretary, Government of India;
Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh
, Director General & CEO, IICA; and
Prof. Garima Dadhich
, Head,
School of Business Environment, IICA
. The session reviewed the principal issues emerging from the two-day deliberations and reflected on the further strengthening of India’s CSR ecosystem through improved governance, institutional coordination, evidence-based planning and greater emphasis on measurable development outcomes.
Shri Ajit Seth
,
former Cabinet Secretary, Government of India
, in his Valedictory Address, emphasised that the success of Corporate Social Responsibility should not be judged only by the quantum of expenditure, but by the difference it made to people’s lives and to the country’s development. He noted that CSR had emerged as a substantial source of development expenditure and observed that the framework had deliberately placed responsibility with company Boards, thereby embedding CSR within the wider evolution of corporate governance and responsible conduct.
He cautioned against tokenism and underlined the need to scale up effective interventions, address geographical imbalances in CSR spending and extend greater attention to underserved districts. He also stressed that technology could strengthen visibility, monitoring and accountability, but could not substitute field knowledge and administrative judgement. Calling upon companies to view CSR not merely as a statutory obligation but as a
strategic instrument for India’s growth
, he said that stronger convergence among stakeholders and sustained attention to inclusive and sustainable outcomes would contribute to the broader vision of
Viksit Bharat @2047
.
Following the Valedictory Address,
Shri Ajit Seth
released the
Compendium of CSR Best Practices 2025
, which brings together the practices showcased by exhibitors during NCCSR 2025. The publication forms part of IICA’s effort to document and disseminate implementation experiences and replicable CSR practices for wider institutional learning.
Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh
, Director General & CEO, IICA, stated that the deliberations during NCCSR 2026 reflected the increasing breadth and maturity of India’s CSR ecosystem. He noted that the Conference had examined issues relating to Board governance, sector-specific CSR approaches, technology and Artificial Intelligence, convergence through the CSR Exchange, women’s economic empowerment, regional distribution of CSR resources, skills and employment, and assessment of social outcomes.
Prof. Garima Dadhich
, Head,
School of Business Environment, IICA
, presented the key outcomes emerging from the Conference and acknowledged the contribution of participating Ministries, public and private sector organisations, international institutions, academia, civil society, exhibitors and delegates.
Earlier in the day, the proceedings commenced with
High-Level Panel on “Transforming CSR through AI & Technology.”
The session examined the use of Artificial Intelligence, digital tools and data systems in the planning, implementation, monitoring and assessment of CSR programmes. It also considered the need for technology adoption to remain anchored in development objectives, accountability and measurable social outcomes. The panel brought together representatives from SBI Foundation, ICICI Bank, HCLFoundation, IndiGo, GIVE and Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham.
At the commencement of the session, the
Compendium of CSR Best Practices showcased at the National Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility 2024
was released. The Compendium documented selected CSR initiatives presented during the previous edition of the National Exhibition, with the objective of facilitating wider dissemination, institutional learning and replication of effective practices.
This was followed by a Keynote Address by
Shri Santanu Mitra
, Senior Economic Adviser,
Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India
. The address considered the evolving role of CSR within the broader framework of responsible business conduct and sustainable development and highlighted the importance of institutional mechanisms that could strengthen the interface between corporate resources, credible social-sector interventions and measurable outcomes.
High-Level Panel discussion on “CSR Exchange: Enabling Convergence, Collaboration and Collective Impact”
examined the role of the CSR Exchange in enabling greater coordination among companies, implementing organisations and other development stakeholders. The session considered issues relating to project visibility, institutional credibility, collaboration and the potential for convergence in addressing development priorities. The panel was chaired by Shri Anil Swarup, former Secretary, Ministry of Coal and Department of School Education and Literacy, Government of India, and moderated by
Prof. Garima Dadhich
. Chairing the panel,  Shri Anil Swarup, former Secretary to the Government of India, remarked that the Portal should meet the expectations set out by the Committee on CSR Exchange. The panel considered how credible information on projects and implementing organisations, transparent processes and stronger institutional coordination could help the Portal fulfil its intended purpose and improve the effectiveness of CSR partnerships.
The panel emphasised the importance of strengthening the CSR Exchange Portal through data integration and automated processes, including mechanisms to facilitate the identification, assessment and selection of credible implementing organisations. It further underscored the need to strengthen the link between CSR expenditure and measurable social development outcomes, particularly through better project assessment, monitoring and reporting. The panel recommended that MCA and IICA should continue to support these priorities through research, capacity building, policy engagement and collaboration among Government, industry and development institutions.
An
Expert Dialogue on “Investing in CARE: Reimagining CSR for Women Economic Empowerment”
examined the relationship between care responsibilities and women’s participation in the economy. The discussion considered the potential for CSR to support childcare, elder care, community-based care infrastructure and skilling of care workers, while strengthening women’s access to employment and economic opportunities. Representatives from SEWA Bharat, Grant Thornton and UN Women participated in the dialogue.
In the afternoon,
High-Level Panel on “Decentralising CSR for Inclusive Regional Growth”
focused on the geographic distribution of CSR resources and the need for interventions to respond more effectively to regional and local development priorities. Representatives from the Department of Public Enterprises, NSE Foundation, Spark Minda Group, Tata Steel Foundation, Inclusion Foundation, Western Coalfields Limited and ONGC Foundation participated in the session.
The panel recommended the development of universal indicators for the assessment of CSR projects, enabling greater consistency and comparability of project outcomes across regions and sectors. It also emphasised that such indicators should be applied with due regard to local circumstances, and that district-level evidence and collaboration with local institutions should inform the identification of priority interventions.
The Conference also featured an
Expert Dialogue on “Leveraging CSR and PMIS – From Skills to Employment”
, with Shri Balamurugan D, Joint Secretary,
Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India
,  Shri Lohit Bhatia, ED & CEO, Quess Corp Ltd, representatives from ONGC and Dixon Technologies India Ltd, moderated by D. Garima Dadhich. Shri Balamurugan D., Joint Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, invited businesses to leverage opportunities under the Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme (PMIS). He highlighted the potential of structured workplace exposure and industry participation to narrow the gap between the skills young people possess and those required for employment. The discussion focused on improving the transition from skilling to employment, strengthening labour-market linkages and exploring the role of CSR in supporting employability and employment outcomes.
The proceedings also included a cultural presentation by artists from the Ministry of Culture before the formal Valedictory Session.
The two-day Conference brought together 600 plus senior representatives from Government, public sector enterprises, private sector companies, international organisations, academia and civil society. The deliberations reinforced the need for CSR interventions to move beyond expenditure and compliance towards stronger governance, evidence-based planning, institutional collaboration and measurable development outcomes, in alignment with national and regional priorities and the vision of
Viksit Bharat
.

title: Raksha Mantri Addresses Participants of Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 at Jodhpur, Emphasises Self-Reliance in Defence and International Cooperation
subtitle:
“Different nations, different aircraft, different experiences, but one sky. That is the message of Tarang Shakti”- Shri Rajnath Singh

“Future military power will be defined by the speed of sensing, understanding, deciding and acting”- RM

“The defence relationships of the future will be about technology and trust, not just about platforms” said RM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 OCT 2026 2:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh addressed the participants of the second edition of Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026 at Air Force Station Jodhpur on October 10, 2026. Hosted by the Indian Air Force (IAF) from 26 September to 12 October 2026, the multinational air exercise brought together air forces from seven Friendly Foreign Countries (FFCs) including Australia, Bangladesh, France, Germany, Sri Lanka, the United Arab Emirates and the United States of America along with 32 observer nations.
Congratulating the IAF and all organisations and personnel involved in the successful conduct of the exercise, the Raksha Mantri welcomed the participating nations and appreciated their contribution to strengthening professional understanding and operational cooperation. He noted that the presence of participating air forces had added significant value to the exercise and expressed hope that the contingents would return with valuable professional insights and a deeper understanding of India's capabilities and perspectives. He highlighted the importance of self-reliance in the defence sector, technological innovation and international partnerships in addressing the evolving challenges of modern warfare.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Rajnath Singh observed that modern warfare was undergoing a profound transformation, extending beyond the traditional domains of land, sea and air to encompass space, cyber, the electromagnetic spectrum and the information domain. He highlighted the growing influence of unmanned systems, drones, artificial intelligence, electronic warfare and long-range precision weapons in shaping contemporary military operations.
“Future military power will be defined less by the number of platforms we possess. It will be determined by the speed of sensing, understanding, deciding, and acting,” he said, underlining that speed, precision, information and integration had emerged as defining attributes of military capability. He also emphasised the need for continuous vigilance in view of the rapidly changing geopolitical environment and the uncertainties associated with technological advancements in the defence sector.
The Raksha Mantri said that India, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, had recognised the importance of strengthening national resilience against emerging security challenges and had adopted Atmanirbharta in defence as a national policy. He stressed that a nation must possess the capability to produce its own weapons and critical technologies to sustain itself during prolonged conflicts and periods of uncertainty.
Highlighting the transformation of the Indian Defence Forces, RM said that the Indian Air Force had evolved from a force operating with limited resources at the time of Independence into a modern aerospace power equipped with advanced aircraft, precision weapons, sophisticated sensors, integrated networks and increasingly advanced indigenous technologies. He emphasised that Atmanirbhar Bharat did not mean isolation from the world, but the development of domestic capabilities to design, develop, manufacture, maintain and upgrade critical defence technologies.
Referring to India's growing aerospace and defence manufacturing ecosystem, the Raksha Mantri highlighted indigenous programmes and systems, including the Tejas fighter aircraft, helicopters such as Dhruv, Rudra, Prachand and the Light Utility Helicopter (LUH), the Akash air defence system, AESA radars, electronic systems, and emerging unmanned and aerospace technologies. RM also referred to the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme as an important step towards mastering fifth-generation stealth fighter technology and underscored the importance of advanced aero-engine development and co-production. He said that India was keen to explore cooperation with like-minded countries in research, co-development, co-production, maintenance, training and innovation. Emphasising the growing importance of trusted partnerships and resilient supply chains, he stated, “The defence relationships of the future will be about technology and trust, not just about platforms.”
The Raksha Mantri observed that building strong indigenous capabilities must go hand in hand with meaningful cooperation with trusted partners. India must be capable of acting independently when required while also operating effectively with other nations when their interests and responsibilities converge, he emphasised.
In this context, RM highlighted the significance of Exercise Tarang Shakti in translating the principles of capability, technology, interoperability and trust into operational experience. The exercise provided participating air forces an opportunity to operate alongside one another, exchange operational knowledge, assess procedures and understand different platforms, doctrines and approaches to mission planning. He noted that multinational exercises enabled aircrews and commanders to learn from one another, examine existing assumptions and identify opportunities to improve their systems and processes.
Describing the spirit of the exercise, Shri Rajnath Singh said, “Different nations. Different aircraft. Different experiences. But one sky. That is the message of Tarang Shakti.” He emphasised that the value of the exercise extended beyond the sorties flown and scenarios practised, encompassing the ability to communicate, coordinate and operate effectively with partner forces. The RM called upon the Indian Air Force to incorporate the lessons of the exercise into its training, tactics, technology, doctrine and future capability development. He expressed confidence that the participating nations would carry forward the professional relationships and mutual understanding developed during the exercise to explore new avenues of aerospace and defence cooperation.
The second edition of Exercise Tarang Shakti builds on the success of its inaugural edition in 2024 and reinforces India's commitment to constructive defence engagement and international cooperation. The exercise brought together diverse combat, transport, surveillance and air-to-air refuelling capabilities, providing opportunities for joint mission planning, operational learning and enhanced interoperability. The participation of indigenous platforms, including the Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas and the Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, also highlighted India's progress in indigenous aerospace design, engineering and manufacturing.
The contemporary relevance of the exercise is underscored by the decisive role of air power in Operation Sindoor, which demonstrated the Indian Air Force’s ability to execute precise, calibrated and effective operations in furtherance of national security objectives. The operation highlighted the importance of operational preparedness, integrated planning, credible deterrence and the effective application of air power in a complex security environment. The experience gained from operational employment reinforces the value of multinational exercises such as Tarang Shakti in advancing professional understanding and preparing for the evolving challenges of modern warfare.
Beyond flying operations, the exercise featured professional engagements, industrial visits and cultural interactions, including yoga sessions, heritage visits and an International Night celebrating the traditions of participating nations. Chief of Defence Staff General N. S. Raja Subramani, Chief of the Air Staff , Air Chief Marshal A P Singh,  Chief of the Naval Staff, Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, other dignitaries,  officials of the Ministry of Defence and participating countries attended the event.

The ABS contributions from the utilisation of agricultural biological resources, including rice, eggplant, cauliflower, cucumber, hot pepper, bottle gourd, bitter gourd, tomato and okra, cover multiple varieties and hybrids. Accordingly, the beneficiary share was apportioned among the concerned State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs) based on the cultivation area of the respective biological resources, as reflected in the agricultural statistics published by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. Of the total ABS amount of Rs 2.02 crore disbursed to 27 SBBs and 3 UTBCs, the top 10 States accounted for Rs 1.43 crore of the total ABS amount.

The ABS mechanism provides an important avenue for mobilising financial resources and channelling them towards biodiversity conservation, sustainable use and local development. Disbursements to State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils support initiatives, including strengthening Biodiversity Management Committees, updating People’s Biodiversity Registers, conserving traditional crop varieties and medicinal plants, restoring habitats, and promoting the sustainable management of biological resources at grassroot level. These measures can further strengthen institutional capacities and enhance the participation of farmers, local communities and other stakeholders in biodiversity governance.
ABS-funded activities can complement relevant Government schemes and programmes, particularly those promoting tribal welfare, sustainable livelihoods and natural-resource-based enterprises, such as the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission and Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana. Such convergence can strengthen community-led conservation, sustainable utilisation of biological resources and livelihood opportunities, while leveraging existing institutional mechanisms
India’s Access and Benefit-Sharing framework contributes to the implementation of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2024–2030. It supports Target 13 of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework on the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilisation of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, as well as Target 19 on resource mobilisation. The framework also contributes to relevant Sustainable Development Goals, including SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), SDG 15 (Life on Land) and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals), through biodiversity conservation, sustainable resource use, livelihood support and institutional collaboration.
As India prepares to participate in the seventeenth meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP 17), commencing on 19 October 2026 in Yerevan, Armenia, its ABS framework demonstrates the country’s continued commitment to biodiversity conservation, the sustainable use of biological resources and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from their utilisation.

A high-level team of Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), under the chairmanship of Dr. S.D. Attri, Member (Technical), CAQM, visited Amritsar and Tarn Taran Districts of Punjab, during the ongoing paddy harvesting season.  These districts have been identified as hotspots for paddy stubble burning. Apart from field visits, the visiting team held a review meeting in Amritsar today (10.10.2026) with Deputy Commissioners (DCs) and other district-level officials of Amritsar and Tarn Taran district. This visit, apart from deployment of Flying Squads, is in line with high priority attached by the Commission towards achieving the objective of reduction and elimination of paddy stubble burning, a major cause of winter air pollution in NCR and adjoining areas.
The deliberations focused on reviewing preparedness and coordination among the concerned departments and district administration for effective
in-situ
and
ex-situ
utilisation of paddy stubble. The Commission stressed upon the importance of facilitating the farmers in terms of timely availability of CRM Machines, sensitizing, conducting Information, Education and Communication (IEC) Activities and providing necessary support.
Along with the review meeting, CAQM undertook field visits on 09.10.2026 and 10.10.2026 to the selected hotspot villages and facilities in districts of Amritsar and Tarn Taran to assess the prevailing ground-level situation and review the implementation of measures aimed at preventing stubble burning.
Regarding the district of Amritsar, the deliberations during the review meeting and field visit included the harvesting and procurement status, along with the availability and deployment of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery. It was informed that balers from Amritsar and adjoining districts were operating for collection and management of paddy straw. A supply chain has been established with industries having boilers for utilisation of paddy straw bales, with farmers and aggregators linked to these industries to facilitate ex-situ management. The district has also established a Control Room and Help Desk at the District Administrative Complex to identify farmers requiring CRM machinery and facilitate its availability. A district-level helpline has been circulated for reporting fire and stubble burning incidents to enable prompt action.
Regarding the district of Tarn Taran, the deliberations during the review meeting and field visit included the harvesting and procurement status and the availability and deployment of CRM machinery in the district. It was informed that balers from Tarn Taran and adjoining districts were operating for effective ex-situ management of paddy straw and that the district had substantially achieved its targets regarding procurement and availability of CRM machinery for farmers. Extensive field patrolling and surveillance through Nodal/ Cluster Officers and other field functionaries, along with IEC Activsties and enforcement measures to promote
in-situ
and
ex-situ
utilistion of paddy straw were also highlighted.
The officers of both districts assured their utmost commitment towards implementation of the CAQM’S Statutory Direction(s), strengthening preventive measures and making concerted efforts to ensure effective prevention of stubble burning incidents in their respective districts.
Additionally, as part of the monitoring mechanism, Flying Squads deputed by the Commission have been deployed in 18 districts across Punjab, namely Sangrur, Tarn Taran, Firozpur, Muktsar, Bathinda, Amritsar, Moga, Mansa, Fazilka, Patiala, Ludhiana, Kapurthala, Faridkot, Barnala, Malerkotla, Gurdaspur, Jalandhar and Fatehgarh Sahib, for the period from 01.10.2026 to 30.11.2026.
CAQM has emphasised the need for continuous and effective field surveillance by District, Nodal and Cluster Officers, particularly in hotspots viz. low-cost sensors and other monitoring mechanisms and enforcement activities must continue without any lapse. Further, it was directed to ensure close coordination among farmers, aggregators, industries and other stakeholders to strengthen the
ex-situ
management supply chain and optimal utilisation of CRM machinery, balers, field staff, surveillance systems and control rooms.
CAQM has been continuously monitoring, coordinating and reviewing the measures being undertaken by the concerned State Governments, State Pollution Control Boards and District Administrations for effective prevention of paddy stubble burning. The Commission has reiterated the need for concerted and coordinated efforts by all concerned agencies, along with active facilitation and cooperation of farmers and other stakeholders, to ensure effective prevention of stubble burning during the ongoing paddy harvesting season.

title: Fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave (KEC 2026) with the theme ‘Resilience in an Age of Flux’ concludes successfully in New Delhi
subtitle: Three-day Conclave brings together policymakers, economists, academics, business leaders and international thought leaders to deliberate on resilience, global fragmentation, technology, trade and India’s economic priorities
date:
Posted On:
                10 OCT 2026 9:25PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Institute of Economic Growth (IEG), in partnership with the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, successfully concluded the Fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave (KEC 2026), held from 3–5 October 2026 in New Delhi under the theme “Resilience in an Age of Flux.” The three-day Conclave brought together more than 200 policymakers, economists, academics, financial experts and international thought leaders, including over 80 international participants from around 30 countries, for high-level discussions on contemporary economic and policy challenges.
The Conclave was inaugurated on 3rd October 2026 by the Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, who delivered the inaugural address. In his address, the Vice-President emphasised that economic resilience cannot be separated from social resilience, highlighting inclusion as a foundation of resilience in a rapidly changing world. He also underlined the importance of policymaking that remains grounded in ground realities and responsive to changing circumstances.
Over three days, the Conclave featured plenary sessions, interactive discussions and focused roundtables examining the challenges and opportunities arising from global economic and geopolitical shifts. Discussions centred on building resilience while sustaining growth, openness and institutional credibility amid recurrent global shocks and uncertainty.
A key highlight of KEC 2026 was the Special Plenary on “Resilience in an Age of Flux: India’s Economic Priorities,” addressed by Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman, Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs, with Ms. Amélie de Montchalin, President of the Cour des Comptes, France, as discussant. The session examined how India can sustain growth, preserve macroeconomic stability and expand investment amid global fragmentation, technological disruption and recurrent shocks, while strengthening the foundations of long-term economic resilience.
The Conclave also brought together significant perspectives on central banking, financial stability and macroeconomic resilience. Discussions examined how monetary authorities can navigate inflation, financial fragility, capital flows and institutional credibility in an environment characterised by recurrent global shocks.
Technology and the digital economy formed another important strand of KEC 2026. Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister for Communications and Minister for Development of North Eastern Region, delivered the keynote address on “Connected India, Empowered Finance: Building Trusted Digital Infrastructure for the AI Economy.” The session examined how digital infrastructure, artificial intelligence and new communication networks can contribute to productivity and economic transformation while maintaining trust and competition.
The Conclave also explored the intersection of culture, heritage and economic development. Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister for Culture and Tourism, delivered the keynote address on “Culture as Capital: From Heritage to Horizons,” examining the role of cultural capital and heritage in the broader architecture of economic development.
The global dimension of the Conclave was further strengthened through discussions on India's evolving position in a changing international order. The special concluding session, “India and the World: Adaptive by Design,” was moderated by Shri N. K. Singh, President, Board of Trustees, IEG. Dr. S. Jaishankar, Union Minister for External Affairs, delivered the special concluding address, with Mr. George Yeo, former Foreign Minister of Singapore, as discussant. The session examined India's strategic autonomy, partnerships and ability to respond flexibly to an increasingly contested and uncertain global environment.
The Conclave's deliberations extended across a broad range of contemporary economic issues, including global fragmentation, trade and supply chains, fiscal and structural reforms, financial markets, development finance, investment, technology and artificial intelligence, employment and skills, demographic change, food systems, sustainability and climate finance. These discussions brought together perspectives from India and across the world, reflecting the Conclave's objective of connecting economic scholarship with policy and global experience.
The Fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave also featured the participation of senior policymakers and leading economic thinkers, including Dr. P. K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister; Shri Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister and former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India; Shri Sanjay Malhotra, Governor, Reserve Bank of India; Smt. Anuradha Thakur, Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs; Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran, Chief Economic Adviser; Lord Nicholas Stern; Professor Michael Greenstone; Jean-Claude Trichet, former President of the European Central Bank; and other eminent Indian and international economists, policymakers and business leaders.
Since its inception in 2022, the Kautilya Economic Conclave has grown into a significant platform for dialogue on contemporary economic and policy challenges. Jointly convened by the Institute of Economic Growth and the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, the Conclave serves as a bridge between scholarship, policymaking and global perspectives. The earlier editions were held under the themes “Redefining the Future” (2022), “Navigating a World on Fire” (2023), “The Indian Era” (2024) and “Seeking Prosperity in Turbulent Times” (2025).
Dr. Michael Debabrata Patra, Chairman, Board of Governors, IEG, and Professor Sabyasachi Kar, Director, IEG, played key roles in guiding and organising the Conclave.
The Fifth Kautilya Economic Conclave reaffirmed the importance of sustained dialogue and evidence-based policymaking in navigating an increasingly complex global environment. Under the theme “Resilience in an Age of Flux,” the Conclave highlighted the need for India and the wider global community to build institutions, policies and partnerships capable of responding to uncertainty while sustaining inclusive growth, investment, innovation and long-term development.

title: Dr. Jitendra Singh Urges Industry to Accelerate Commercialisation of Indian Innovation, Scale Up Capabilities for Strategic Sovereignty by 2047
subtitle:
Union Minister calls for stronger industry participation to translate scientific research into commercial ventures and globally competitive technologies

India achieves 1,000 km of quantum-secure communication against an eight-year target of 2,000 km: Dr. Jitendra Singh

India’s Bioeconomy Exceeds US 195 billion; Target Set atUS300 Billion by 2030, Says Dr. Jitendra Singh

At PHDCCI’s 121st Annual Session, Minister stresses stronger public-private synergy to realise India’s technology ambitions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 OCT 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Industry must come forward to accelerate innovation, translate scientific research into commercial ventures and scale up India’s technological capabilities to achieve the national objectives set for 2047 and strengthen the country’s strategic sovereignty, said Dr. Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space.
Addressing the 121st Annual Session of the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI) in New Delhi today, the Minister emphasised the need to bring Government, industry, academia, research institutions and start-ups together to convert scientific capabilities into indigenous technologies, commercially viable enterprises and globally competitive solutions. Held at New Delhi, the session brought together industry leaders, entrepreneurs and other stakeholders to discuss India’s growth and innovation priorities.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s next phase of technological growth must move beyond the adoption of technologies developed elsewhere towards creating indigenous solutions with global relevance. The expansion of the space ecosystem following policy reforms, alongside greater private-sector participation in strategic technology areas, demonstrates the opportunities that emerge when scientific capabilities are supported by an enabling policy environment and entrepreneurial initiative.
Citing progress under the National Quantum Mission, the Minister said India had set an eight-year target of achieving 2,000 kilometres of quantum-secure communication and had achieved the 1,000-kilometre milestone in three years, according to his address. He emphasised the strategic and security significance of quantum communication and the importance of developing domestic capabilities in frontier technologies.
The Minister also referred to the growth of India’s bioeconomy from around US10 billion in 2014 to approximately US196 billion, with an ambition to reach US$300 billion by 2030. He cited the expansion of the biotechnology start-up ecosystem as evidence of the opportunities emerging in life sciences and advanced research. These developments, he said, demonstrate the potential of scientific innovation to generate new enterprises, strengthen domestic capabilities and create economic value.
Dr. Jitendra Singh stressed that industry engagement should begin at the inception of research projects, enabling scientists to understand market requirements, identify technological needs and develop solutions with a clear pathway to commercial deployment. Industry bodies such as PHDCCI can play an important role in connecting researchers with businesses, facilitating investment and building partnerships that help innovations progress from laboratories to prototypes and market-ready products.
Referring to the Government’s Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) initiative, the Minister said greater private-sector participation in research and development was essential to accelerate the translation of scientific discoveries into commercial applications. He encouraged industry to participate more actively in research-led innovation and help build an ecosystem in which scientific excellence leads to sustainable enterprises and globally competitive products.
The Minister also stressed the importance of indigenous technologies and reliable energy supplies for India’s ambitions in artificial intelligence, data infrastructure and advanced manufacturing. Developing domestic capabilities in strategic and emerging technologies, alongside deeper collaboration between industry and scientific institutions, would be essential to strengthening India’s technological self-reliance and strategic sovereignty.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s next leap would depend on combining new thinking with faster execution and the ability to scale successful innovations. Stronger partnerships among Government, industry, academia and start-ups would help accelerate commercialisation, expand the country’s innovation base and build the technological capabilities required to realise India’s ambitions for 2047.
